# Labelled by a subagent denied the classifier's source, the iteration reports and the earlier
# label fixtures; it read the criterion and the sample and nothing else.
# This fixture is never regenerated: a session is not reproducible, so the labels are the artifact
# and not the process that made them.
# Families labelled under criterion rules a future revision might supersede:

# - Product managers: Staff Product Manager Ads Signals, Product Manager Logs Observability, Associate Product Manager. Labelled UNKNOWN scope_ambiguity as a ruled phrase whose variants split on Q4, even with a software qualifier, so step 5 never fired for them; a ruling that product manager is (or is not) engineering-capable under Q4 would flip the whole family to IN or OUT.

# - Other managers and project managers: Project Manager Value Delivery Enterprise AI, Manager Software Engineering Billing, Manager Computer System Validation QA (IN at step 5, manager read as engineering-capable); Operations Manager, Project Management Consultant (OUT at step 6, the unclassed modifier read as a market marker); Manager of Engineering, Engineering Manager Product Engineering (UNKNOWN domain_ambiguity). A revision declaring manager not engineering-capable would move the IN rows to unruled.

# - Sales and presales engineers: Sales Engineer II Dedrone, Pre Sales Systems Engineer Enterprise, Solutions Engineer, Regional Field CTO, Customer Success Engineer. UNKNOWN scope_ambiguity by Q4 judgement rather than OUT at step 6 with sales as a market marker; Value Engineer Public Sector was read literally and is OUT. A ruling on sales engineer either way flips the family.

# - AI-training gig posts: Computer Sciences Graduates AI Training, AI Engineer ML Engineer Developers AI Training, Javascript Developers AI Training (IN, software qualifier and Q4); Fluent Kannada Speakers AI Training, Neuroscience AI Training (OUT, language or discipline); AI Training Experts Arizona, Canada Residents AI Trainers (UNKNOWN domain_ambiguity). A ruling that these posts fail Q1 or never pass Q2-Q4 would move the IN rows to OUT.

# - Engineer or technician with an unclassed modifier: Engineer Total Product Support, Field Service Engineer, Value Engineer (OUT at step 6, unclassed modifier as market marker) against Test Engineer, Systems Engineer V Test, QA QC Engineer, Lab Engineer II, Modeling Simulation Engineer, Systems Operations Engineer (UNKNOWN domain_ambiguity, because systems, test, QA, validation, simulation and lab were read as possibly-software and not as market). Classing those words as software qualifiers or as market markers would flip them to IN or OUT.

# - Hardware-adjacent code roles without a named discipline: GPU Engineer, Hardware Machine Learning Engineer, Debug Validation Engineer, 2026 Fall Intern SOC Modeling. UNKNOWN domain_ambiguity per the criterion's FPGA paragraph; Silicon Engineer, RF Engineer, ASIC Physical Design Engineer, UAS Systems Integration Engineer were ruled OUT at step 4 with silicon, RF, ASIC and UAS read as discipline markers. Classing hardware or GPU as a discipline marker would flip the first group to OUT.

# - Vendor-package analysts: Epic Referrals Analyst, Specialist Epic Solution Delivery, EBS Analyst, ServiceNow Business Analyst, Lead SAP Business Solutions S4 Hana (UNKNOWN scope_ambiguity), against SAP Basis Admin and Calypso CATT Specialist (IN, as technical administration and test automation). A ruling that a named enterprise package is a software qualifier under Q3 would flip the scope rows to IN.

# - Domain-free heads under non-engineering markets: Content Moderation Analyst, Underwriting Analyst, Treasury Operations Analyst, Architect K 12, Customer Success Architect. UNKNOWN domain_ambiguity by the Treasury Analyst rule even where the title reads plainly non-engineering; Actuarial Analyst and Logistician Data Analyst are OUT (actuarial as a discipline marker, logistician as the first head). A reclass of analyst or architect as domain-bound, as happened to consultant, would move most of this family to OUT.
